title: Most news apps treat you like a demographic, not a reader.
body:
When you sign up for a news service, it usually asks you to pick topics like 'tech' or 'politics.' But that is a clumsy way to understand what you actually care about. A person who loves space exploration might hate reading about corporate mergers, even if both fall under the broad umbrella of business or tech.

At Headlinne, we built an engine that learns differently. It does not just track what you click. It observes how you engage with the nuance of a story. It notices when you consistently read deep-dive analysis versus quick updates. It learns the specific writers or perspectives you trust, not just the keywords you search for.

The goal is to build a feed that feels like it was curated by an editor who knows your taste perfectly. It is not about keeping you scrolling for hours. It is about making sure that the time you do spend reading is actually worth it.

We believe technology should respect your attention span, not exploit it. Learning your preferences takes time, but it results in a news experience that feels human rather than algorithmic.
cta: You can experience how it works for yourself at HEADLINNE.com.
